_comment: Predicate registry. 'single_valued' predicates auto-retire a prior object during kb_extract consolidation, but only when the subject matches 'single_valued_subjects' — cardinality is a property of (subject, predicate), not of the predicate. A ticket has one status; a repo accumulates them. Everything else keeps both objects. The subject pattern requires a separator or # before the trailing digits, so ticket and issue ids (tkt-4821, pr_#3583, svc-api#59) match while names that merely end in a digit (web3, oauth2, sqlite3, es2022) do not. 'aliases' fold synonyms onto one canonical predicate so kb_fact_query, which matches on the predicate, does not under-return across synonym silos. 'inverses' fold the mirrored spelling of a relationship onto one direction, swapping subject and object — the extractor picks a direction per call, and two live rows for one relationship retire independently. Each direction here is the one the graph already uses more, and none of them are single-valued, so the fold cannot change what retires what. Extend or override per install with <KB_DIR>/predicates.json using the same shape — 'many_valued' there removes a built-in, 'aliases' and 'inverses' merge with these, and 'single_valued_subjects' replaces this pattern.
